about: Every day of 2026 on which the engine, with the United States and FSSP layers, differs from the FSSP seminary's page (fsspolgs.org/liturgical-calendar, read 2026-11-09) on celebration, class or commemorations, and how it differs. The first printed row is scored; where that row is another Mass, the row for the day's own celebration is scored as well. The page is not in this repository; set FSSP_PAGE to a saved copy to re-check.

groups.why: The page prints first a Mass the ordo permits beside the day's own: First Friday and First Saturday votives, the Requiem of November, the Rogation Mass, a Mass for certain places, or a commemorated saint taken as the Mass of a 4th class day. Where the page also prints the day's own celebration lower down, that row is compared too ('own row'). These belong to the Masses an ordo offers, not to the calendar: src/ordo.ts gives each of them, and test/fixtures/fssp-2026-masses.json scores the page's first row against the FSSP ordo's first Mass.
groups.note: On 27 June, 4 July and 5 November the day's own row commemorates a Mass for certain places (Our Lady of Perpetual Help, All Holy Popes, Holy Relics); see the next group. On 5 December the first row commemorates the Advent feria because the Mass is a votive one.

groups.group: a Mass for certain places commemorated on the feria
groups.why: The page adds to the feria's row a commemoration of a Mass for certain places that it also offers as the Mass of the day. These are not in the universal calendar, the United States proper or the Fraternity's (data/ordos/fssp.json lists them as Masses the ordo offers): the French district's ordo prints a plain feria on both dates, and the SSPX Ordo has no commemoration. src/ordo.ts offers them as Masses of the day; it does not commemorate them.

groups.why: The same commemorations in another order. The engine follows no. 113: the season first, then the table of precedence, then the calendar's own order. On 1 September and 21 October that is the order the calendar lists the two saints in; on 4 December the page's own second row has the engine's order. 27 March stays unresolved (README): the page puts the Seven Sorrows first, the SSPX Ordo and the engine put St. John Damascene first.

groups.group: the page differs from the rubrics
groups.why: 1 January: the Octave of Christmas is printed as 2nd class; it is 1st (no. 91 item 5). 11 January: the Holy Family is printed as 1st class with the Sunday commemorated; it is 2nd class and the Sunday is not commemorated (no. 17b). 28 June: the Vigil of Sts. Peter and Paul is commemorated on a Sunday; a vigil of the 2nd class is omitted on a Sunday (no. 33). 8 September: St. Hadrian is not commemorated; a 2nd class feast admits one commemoration (no. 111c), and the SSPX Ordo prints him. 16 and 17 December: the 'Feria of Advent' is commemorated on Advent days that are themselves of the season (no. 112c).

groups.group: the Fraternity's own feast is not on the page
groups.why: The Chair of St. Peter is of the 1st class in the Fraternity (data/layers/fssp.json). On 22 February 2026 it met the 1st Sunday of Lent, so it is kept on Monday 23 February (no. 96) with the Lenten feria commemorated (nos. 109e, 111a); St. Peter Damian, a 3rd class feast, is not commemorated on a 1st class day. The page prints the feria and St. Peter Damian, as the universal calendar has them.
